brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: All three keyhole hangers (accessory:0#-1,0#4, 0#0,0#4, 0#1,0#4) sit on the same side of the row, so it can hang on screws already in the wall. How much weight they hold isn't something the configurator checks.
Three bins with 3 compartments each: bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0 and bin:1,0,0 (9 compartments in all).
Three hex-acc-keyhole accessories, one on each cell, all on slot 4.

finish.summary: I built a spice rack from three hex cells side by side in one row, at q = -1, 0 and 1. Each cell holds a full-depth bin with 3 compartments, so there are 9 spots for spice jars. A keyhole hanger is fitted on slot 4 of each cell. That puts all three on the same side, the face left uncapped in every cell, which is the side that goes against the wall. The other open faces have end caps, and the two joints between cells are bolted. The check came back with no rule issues and no mesh clashes ("clear"). The prop catalogue has no spice jars and the kitchen props in it don't suit a spice rack, so I didn't stage any props in the bins. The configurator only checks fit, so it can't say how much weight the hangers or plastic will hold on the wall.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
